First-year builders with zero fear and full momentum.

We are a team of passionate freshers combining rapid learning, creative problem-solving, and clean execution. What we lack in years, we make up for in curiosity, late-night grit, and a drive to build practical, real-world solutions.
summary:
POLAR WINDOW is a full-stack 3D lunar mission planning dashboard and surface simulation built with FastAPI, NASA SPICE, React, and Three.js.

Mission Portal: Opens with an interactive 3D Moon landing page featuring capability overviews, a site catalog, and "Try Polar Window" launch buttons that enter the live command center.
NASA SPICE & LOLA Backend: Uses real NASA NAIF SPICE DE440 ephemerides (MOON_ME frame) and LRO LOLA topography across 17 calibrated lunar sites (Shackleton, Cabeus, Shoemaker, Haworth, Nobile VIPER, Malapert, Taurus-Littrow, Shiv Shakti, etc.) to compute solar elevation, vacuum horizon dip, solar array power, battery state-of-charge, Direct-to-Earth comms, and autonomous landing safety scores.
3D Lunar Globe & LOLA Craters: Displays high-contrast LOLA crater rim contours, PSR water-ice cold-trap basins, Sun/Earth vectors, and a docked LOLA DEM altimetry HUD without cluttering the globe with moving tags.
3D Apollo Lunar Rover (LRV) Simulator: Features photorealistic craters, fractured boulders (including Tracy's Rock), 4-wheel independent suspension that climbs over rocks, lunar gravity (

dataRefs: NASA NAIF SPICE Kernels (JPL Ephemerides): de440s.bsp: JPL Developmental Ephemeris 440 for high-precision planetary, Sun, Earth, and Moon state vectors with light-time and stellar aberration (LT+S). moon_pa_de440_200625.bpc & moon_de440_250416.tf: Lunar Principal Axes (MOON_PA) and Mean Earth/Polar Axis (MOON_ME) orientation frames. pck00011.tpc & naif0012.tls: IAU planetary constants ( 𝑅 Moon = 1737.4  km R Moon 	​  =1737.4 km) and UTC-to-Ephemeris Time (ET) leapseconds. NASA JPL Horizons System API: Live REST cross-validation (ssd.jpl.nasa.gov/api/horizons.api) for topocentric observer solar & Earth azimuth/elevation angles. NASA LRO LOLA (Lunar Orbiter Laser Altimeter) DEM: South Polar Digital Elevation Model (LDEM_80S,  5  m 5 m– 20  m/px 20 m/px) calibrated elevation ( ℎ h), rim height, floor depth, terrain slope ( deg deg), and Permanently Shadowed Region (PSR) boundaries across 17 lunar sites (Artemis III candidates, VIPER Nobile Rim, Apollo 17 Taurus-Littrow, and Chandrayaan-3 Shiv Shakti). LRO Diviner & LCROSS Volatile Data: Cryogenic cold-trap temperatures ( < 40  K <40 K to  110  K 110 K) and water-ice regolith indicators. NASA LRO WAC Basemaps & Apollo 17 LRV Specs: LRO Wide Angle Camera albedo/normal relief maps and authentic Apollo 17 Lunar Roving Vehicle dimensions, wire-mesh wheels, and  1.62  m/s 2 1.62 m/s 2  lunar gravity physics.
